title: Barygaza the Silver Port
subtitle: Where the Silver Tide Met the Saka Road
era: Indian Ocean trade under Nahapana, c. 1st century CE
region: Bharuch, Gulf of Khambhat and western trade routes
moral: Trade thrives where rulers protect routes and merchants earn trust.

sources.citation: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, sections 41-49, translated by W. H. Schoff, 1912; Lionel Casson edition, 1989
sources.note: Primary external merchant account of Barygaza's imports, exports and difficult tides.

sources.citation: Nasik cave inscriptions of Ushavadata, in D. C. Sircar, Select Inscriptions, vol. 1, 1965
sources.note: Primary evidence for rest-houses, cisterns and route patronage at Bharuch, Sopara and related nodes.

sources.citation: Himanshu Prabha Ray, The Winds of Change: Buddhism and the Maritime Links of Early South Asia, Oxford University Press, 1994
sources.note: Connects maritime trade, ports and cave patronage in western India.

panels.shot: sweeping aerial over a crowded ancient port at dusk

dialogue.text: In Nahapana’s time, at Barygaza on the roaring gulf, Saka satraps, inland roads and foreign winds met in silver, cotton and risk.

panels.shot: low, wide shot from ship’s prow entering estuary

dialogue.text: The Periplus begins with a warning: the approach to Barygaza is perilous, its tides swift, its shoals treacherous, and only local pilots know the safe path upriver.

panels.shot: medium close-up on Merchant of Barygaza, wind in his hair

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Steady your hands. This river has drowned men who thought coin could tame it.

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Bharuch from the river

dialogue.text: Beyond the tides lies Bharukaccha, Barygaza, a port of the Western Kshatrapas under the Saka satrap Nahapana, where sea routes end and caravan roads begin.

panels.shot: interior wide of a bustling warehouse by the river

dialogue.text: The Periplus lists the port’s wealth: cotton cloth from the Deccan, rice from fertile fields, sesame oil and ghee, indigo, onyx and other stones, all gathered in warehouse shade.

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Each bale is a promise—from farmer to weaver to sea and back.

panels.shot: medium shot of foreign traders entering warehouse

dialogue.text: From the Red Sea came traders the Periplus calls Yavana, bringing wine in amphorae, copper, tin, lead, coral, and above all gold and silver coin to exchange.

panels.shot: close-up on a spread of coins and goods on a low table

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Your coin buys cloth, oil and colour. But our trust weighs more than metal.

panels.shot: wide shot of caravans forming outside city gate

dialogue.text: Barygaza is not only a harbour. It is a hinge. From here, caravans roll inland toward markets and cities whose precise lines the earth has blurred.

panels.shot: stylised map-like overhead showing sea and inland routes

dialogue.text: The Periplus names inland centres like Minnagara, their exact locations now debated, reminding us how even trade giants can fade into the mist of argument and guesswork.

panels.shot: low-angle shot of a Saka official at a road post

dialogue.text: On land, inscriptions of Nahapana’s son-in-law Ushavadata speak of rest-houses, cisterns and gifts along the very routes that feed Barygaza, tying satrap power to merchant roads.

panels.shot: medium shot focused on a stone cistern by the roadside

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: A full cistern and a shaded bench add more to trade than a drawn sword.

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a rock-cut cave monastery

dialogue.text: Cave inscriptions at places like Nasik record donations from satrap families and merchants, showing how the same wealth that moved along roads also carved stone refuges for the renunciants.

panels.shot: close-up on carved inscription being traced by fingers

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Stone keeps names longer than ledgers. But names too can sink.

panels.shot: busy street-level shot inside Bharuch’s bazaar

dialogue.text: Himanshu Prabha Ray sees in such ports a web: maritime links, road-side shrines, cave monasteries, all threaded together by merchants who live between wind, tax and trust.

panels.shot: evening wide shot on the riverfront with ships at anchor

dialogue.text: As the tide turns gentle and masts darken against the sky, the Periplus notes that this difficult harbour rewards patience, and that satrap rule has made its roads secure enough for risk to seem worth it.

panels.shot: close-up on Merchant of Barygaza holding coins and a ledger

dialogue.speaker: Merchant of Barygaza
dialogue.text: Today’s silver may come from far seas. Tomorrow’s trust must be earned here.

panels.shot: high, contemplative shot of the port fading into mist over time

dialogue.text: Today the exact paths to places like Minnagara are disputed, yet the record of Barygaza remains: a port where Saka satraps, river pilots and merchants together turned dangerous tides into lasting routes.

panels.shot: final medium shot of Merchant of Barygaza on the quay at dawn

dialogue.text: In the story of Barygaza, we see that trade endures where rulers guard routes, merchants keep faith across cultures, and the hardest currents are faced together, not alone.
